notes: StarWars.com records Ben Burtt’s electronic-and-human construction of R2-D2’s expressive voice, and the official Databank binds R2-D2 to Star Wars: A New Hope.
Disney’s 2008 slate identifies Ben Burtt as WALL·E’s Sound and Character Voice Designer, while Pixar identifies the exact character and image family.

The first discovery artifact failed visual second desk because its R2-D2 hero crop omitted both side-leg endings, the center foot, and the complete silhouette. Those rejected bytes remain permanently named and forbidden.

The first permanent-apply run materialized and checksummed 17 files but failed before gate, commit, or push because it measured the staged retirement delta against the temporary apply head instead of the UC-174 base; its untyped custody packet remains rejected.
The repair orbit retained 88 byte-distinct candidates from the official Lucasfilm R2-D2 Biography Gallery. The selected direct object is the untransformed raw URL, not its CDN region derivative.

The selected R2-D2 frame preserves the dome, torso panels, both side legs, both side feet, center foot, and complete design silhouette. C-3PO is secondary and does not obscure or substitute for R2-D2.
The held Pixar WALL·E bytes remain unchanged and preserve the binocular eyes, neck, chassis, nameplate, arms, hands, cube, and tread assemblies.
Each 624x1000 panel contains a 560-pixel identity region and a 432-pixel centered full-source region separated by an eight-pixel rule. A twelve-pixel divider prevents role bleed-through.
The 1246x1000 wall simulation removes seven pixels from each outside field without changing either identity region, full-source view, role, chronology, or source edge.
The existing Ben Burtt performer portrait remains unchanged and outside the still packet’s asserted object.
Exact-byte duplicate screening passes against 2,070 canonical repository hashes.
